note_sections.t: Re-evaluation of prostate cancer management options following confirmed Gleason 4+3 diagnosis and rising PSA trend.

Recently retired postal worker with a history of type 2 diabetes, coronary artery disease, and chronic kidney disease. He is married and lives with his partner, with his adult son as primary contact. He continues to run 3 times per week for 5 km despite mobility limitations requiring a frame. Alcohol consumption is moderate at 6 units per week. He reports moderate lower urinary tract symptoms with an IPSS score of 13/35. His PSA has fluctuated, rising from 1.3 ng/mL in July 2023 to 5.3 ng/mL in December 2023, then dropping to 1.1 ng/mL in May 2024 before rising again to 5.4 ng/mL in September 2024 and 5.5 ng/mL in February 2025. He is currently on metformin, empagliflozin, aspirin, atorvastatin, and metoprolol.

On DRE, the prostate is non-palpable and no nodules or asymmetry are detected, consistent with clinical stage cT1c. General examination reveals stable vital signs with BP 127/99 mmHg and HR 78 bpm. Patient uses a frame for mobility but is otherwise well-nourished with BMI 31.0.

admin: Mobility limitation (frame); ground-floor consult room preferred.
